nodes.Name: Protocols
nodes.DocComment:
Protocols is a set of HTTP protocols.
The zero value is an empty set of protocols.

The supported protocols are:

  - HTTP1 is the HTTP/1.0 and HTTP/1.1 protocols.
    HTTP1 is supported on both unsecured TCP and secured TLS connections.

  - HTTP2 is the HTTP/2 protcol over a TLS connection.

  - UnencryptedHTTP2 is the HTTP/2 protocol over an unsecured TCP connection.

nodes.Name: HTTP1
nodes.DocComment: HTTP1 reports whether p includes HTTP/1.

nodes.Name: SetHTTP1
nodes.DocComment: SetHTTP1 adds or removes HTTP/1 from p.

nodes.Name: HTTP2
nodes.DocComment: HTTP2 reports whether p includes HTTP/2.

nodes.Name: SetHTTP2
nodes.DocComment: SetHTTP2 adds or removes HTTP/2 from p.

nodes.Name: UnencryptedHTTP2
nodes.DocComment: UnencryptedHTTP2 reports whether p includes unencrypted HTTP/2.

nodes.Name: SetUnencryptedHTTP2
nodes.DocComment: SetUnencryptedHTTP2 adds or removes unencrypted HTTP/2 from p.

nodes.Name: incomparable
nodes.DocComment:
incomparable is a zero-width, non-comparable type. Adding it to a struct
makes that struct also non-comparable, and generally doesn't add
any size (as long as it's first).

nodes.Name: maxInt64
nodes.DocComment:
maxInt64 is the effective "infinite" value for the Server and
Transport's byte-limiting readers.

nodes.Name: aLongTimeAgo
nodes.DocComment:
aLongTimeAgo is a non-zero time, far in the past, used for
immediate cancellation of network operations.

nodes.Name: omitBundledHTTP2
nodes.DocComment:
omitBundledHTTP2 is set by omithttp2.go when the nethttpomithttp2
build tag is set. That means h2_bundle.go isn't compiled in and we
shouldn't try to use it.

nodes.Name: contextKey
nodes.DocComment:
contextKey is a value for use with context.WithValue. It's used as
a pointer so it fits in an interface{} without allocation.

nodes.Name: hasPort
nodes.DocComment:
Given a string of the form "host", "host:port", or "[ipv6::address]:port",
return true if the string includes a port.

nodes.Name: removeEmptyPort
nodes.DocComment:
removeEmptyPort strips the empty port in ":port" to ""
as mandated by RFC 3986 Section 6.2.3.

nodes.Name: isToken
nodes.DocComment: isToken reports whether v is a valid token (https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc2616#section-2.2).

nodes.Name: stringContainsCTLByte
nodes.DocComment: stringContainsCTLByte reports whether s contains any ASCII control character.

nodes.Name: NoBody
nodes.DocComment:
NoBody is an [io.ReadCloser] with no bytes. Read always returns EOF
and Close always returns nil. It can be used in an outgoing client
request to explicitly signal that a request has zero bytes.
An alternative, however, is to simply set [Request.Body] to nil.

nodes.Name: PushOptions
nodes.DocComment: PushOptions describes options for [Pusher.Push].

nodes.Name: Pusher
nodes.DocComment:
Pusher is the interface implemented by ResponseWriters that support
HTTP/2 server push. For more background, see
https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc7540#section-8.2.

nodes.Name: HTTP2Config
nodes.DocComment:
HTTP2Config defines HTTP/2 configuration parameters common to
both [Transport] and [Server].
